story.sq07.title: Thirteen Empty Spaces
story.sq07.summary: Trace the emergency renewals, distinguish authorization from consent, and make the evidence accessible without exposing unrelated households.
story.sq07.s1.objective: Read three representative renewal sheets and compare their blank handover fields.
story.sq07.s1.journal: Year one promised a survey. Year six cited stable operation. Year twelve cited the cost of replacement. Each renewed the emergency, but none contains Shen’s consent or a named successor. Main records already prove his original limit; these sheets explain how it was ignored.
story.sq07.s1.lan: I blamed a faceless council because that was easier than reading the signatures. Some signed to keep the next flood away. They still signed an obligation that was not theirs.
story.sq07.s1.apprentice: We can record their reasons without turning a renewal into Shen’s permission.
story.sq07.s1.note: Renewal extracts: Year 1—“Survey replacement before the next wet season.” Year 6—“No present instability; defer expenditure.” Year 12—“Relocation estimate exceeds reserve; extend existing governor.” All three carry approval stamps. All three leave the affected warden’s consent and successor blank. Attached household lists contain addresses unrelated to the governor decision.
story.sq07.s2.objective: Arrange the three dated renewals and choose an evidence-access format.
story.sq07.s2.journal: Public summary copies can show decisions, signatory roles, dates, and missing consent without household addresses. Alternatively, supervised facsimiles keep full decision pages available on-site while personal attachments remain protected. Neither option erases an original.
story.sq07.s2.lan: Anyone below should be able to ask why this lasted thirteen years. They should not have to publish where their children sleep to ask it.
story.sq07.s2.clue: Approval stamps validate that an office authorized a renewal; they do not fill the separate consent box. Align Year 1, Year 6, and Year 12, then mark each blank consent field. Keep the household attachment under its existing cover.
story.sq07.s2.choice_a: Post public summaries and an index to preserved originals.
story.sq07.s2.choice_b: Open supervised decision-page copies with protected attachments.
story.sq07.s2.reply_a: The summaries will include the missing consent and the signatory roles. The index will say where the originals can be inspected.
story.sq07.s2.reply_b: The decision pages will stay readable here. We will log access to personal attachments instead of pretending they must all be public.
story.sq07.s3.objective: Verify the access notice preserves the original limit, missing consents, and archive locations.
story.sq07.s3.journal: The archive now separates the reason for a decision from consent to bear its cost. No public format can undo thirteen years. A later reviewer will at least have the actual dates and unfilled fields.
story.sq07.s3.lan: Leave my bypass ledger in the index too. I do not get to demand their records and hide the one with my tool marks.
story.sq07.s3.apprentice: The bypass is indexed, with its date and limits. It will not be used to excuse the old renewals or erase what you changed.
story.sq07.s3.record: Access notice: original governor term thirty days; later approvals did not supply recorded renewed consent; successor fields unfilled. Available records: governor agreement, Years 1/6/12 renewals, Yun’s calculations, Lan’s dated bypass ledger. Household addresses are not displayed. Originals retained. Corrections must be dated and appended, never silently substituted.
story.sq07.s3.retry: A date, missing-consent mark, or archive location is unchecked. Compare the notice against the originals; no additional expedition is necessary.
story.sq07.s3.done: Archive access established. Original evidence and personal attachments remain preserved.
story.sq07.epilogue.open: At the next seasonal review, a copied renewal is challenged in public. The apprentice’s temporary regulation now has a dated question beside it: who replaces this burden, and when?
story.sq07.epilogue.seal: The retired sanctuary keeps its accessible archive. Giving up the array’s power does not erase the approvals that sustained it; displaced households can still inspect the record.
story.sq07.epilogue.shared: The first proposed renewal arrives with an expiry date and signed duty consents. Someone still checks the blanks. The old archive remains open precisely because the new charter can also fail.
